feed.title: Swop Journal
feed.subtitle: Product, markets and engineering notes from Swop.

entry.title: Copy trading on Solana: how it works and where it goes wrong
entry.summary: Copy trading mirrors someone else's public wallet into yours. Here is what you are delegating, why your fill is never their fill, and what to check before you copy anyone.

entry.title: Stablecoins are the tokenization that already won
entry.summary: Stablecoins already hold more on-chain value than every other tokenized real-world asset combined — about $290B against about $32–48B total.

entry.title: What happens if a tokenized asset’s issuer fails?
entry.summary: If the issuer of a tokenized real-world asset fails, what you recover depends on the legal structure behind the token, not the blockchain it runs on.

entry.title: Somebody made gold in a reactor
entry.summary: A fusion startup says it transmuted mercury into gold. The amounts are trivial and the tonnage is simulated — but it exposes what gold's scarcity always rested on, and why rule-based scarcity is a different thing entirely.

entry.title: Remittances: the real test for tokenized money
entry.summary: Stablecoins cross a border in seconds, but a remittance isn't done until that balance becomes spendable cash — and that leg hasn't gotten faster.

entry.title: Starbucks runs a $1.7 billion float on gift cards
entry.summary: Prepaid store credit is the most underrated product in retail — it funds the business and brings people back in person. Geo Bucks, Drops and Launchpad put the same mechanic behind any counter.

entry.title: El Dorado is live in beta
entry.summary: El Dorado is a virtual world built on Swop. You sign in with your swop.id — a wallet you hold the keys to — and you can pair a VR headset. It's in beta, and it ships improvements every week.

entry.title: Tokenized isn’t the same as yours
entry.summary: Tokenized real-world assets passed $32 billion in 2026 — and the largest category reverts if you send it to a wallet nobody approved. Custody, not the chain, decides who gets to participate.

entry.title: Settlement is the product
entry.summary: T+2 is not a technology limit. It is an artifact of netting, reconciliation and intermediaries — and removing it changes who gets to use their own money, and when.

entry.title: The unbanked don’t need a bank. They need a ledger.
entry.summary: 1.3 billion adults have no financial account while 86% own a phone. That gap is not technology — it is unit economics. Tokenization is what changes the math.

entry.title: How to accept crypto payments as a freelancer
entry.summary: A freelancer can accept crypto payments with a self-custody wallet and a payment link — no bank, merchant account, or ID check on the crypto rail.

entry.title: Sell digital products for crypto: how it works
entry.summary: Selling digital products for crypto means pricing them in a stablecoin and getting paid on-chain the moment the sale settles — no processor, no payout delay.

entry.title: What is a wrapped token? A claim on a bridge, not the issuer
entry.summary: A wrapped token represents another asset on a different chain, minted when a bridge locks the original. It's a claim on the bridge, not on the original issuer.

entry.title: How does Swop make money? The 0.5% fee, explained
entry.summary: Swop's only published revenue source is a 0.5% SwopPay checkout fee. Here's what it covers, and which parts of the business aren't priced in public yet.

entry.title: Best wallet for prediction markets: what to check
entry.summary: The best wallet for prediction markets is self-custodial, keeps gas off your plate, and shows full order-book depth. Here's the full checklist to run first.

entry.title: Recover a crypto wallet without a seed phrase: what actually works
entry.summary: Losing a seed phrase usually means losing the funds. Here is what recovery without one actually requires, what it trades away, and how to check a wallet's model before you need it.

entry.title: Email gave the internet an account. It never gave it a wallet.
entry.summary: Email made accounts universal but left them inert. The next primitive is an identity that carries money and can prove one fact without disclosing who you are — which is what ZeroProof, still in development, is being built for.

entry.title: Solana wallet with a built-in swap: why it matters
entry.summary: A Solana wallet with a built-in swap lets you trade tokens inside the app instead of bridging out to an exchange first. Here's what changes, and what to check.

entry.title: Self-custody crypto wallet in Bangladesh: what the law says
entry.summary: A self-custody wallet means you hold the keys, not a bank. In Bangladesh, trading in cryptocurrency is banned outright — here's what that means.

entry.title: Tokenizing real-world assets: treasuries, gold, stocks, and collectibles
entry.summary: Tokenizing a real-world asset means issuing a token backed by a redemption right on something off-chain — a Treasury bill, gold bar, stock, or luxury good.

entry.title: The CLARITY Act vote: what happened, and what the bill actually does
entry.summary: The Senate cloture vote failed 49-50 on September 15, 2026. The SEC and CFTC have built an alternative out of rulemaking — and why that is not the same as a law for capital and for builders.

entry.title: Cross-chain swap wallet: how swapping between chains actually works
entry.summary: A cross-chain swap moves value between two separate blockchains that cannot talk to each other. Here is what actually happens under the hood, and what to check before you trust one.

entry.title: AI agents and your wallet: a safety checklist
entry.summary: A wallet lets an AI agent trade safely only when it can't sign without your approval, holds no keys itself, bounds its authority, and logs every decision.

entry.title: Send crypto with a link (no wallet address needed)
entry.summary: You can send crypto to someone with a shareable link instead of a wallet address — they claim it into their own wallet when they open it. Here's how it works.

entry.title: What is a SmartSite? A crypto profile page, explained
entry.summary: A SmartSite is a crypto profile page at your own swop.id handle: tabbed sections holding links, media, posts and products — and it can take payments directly.

entry.title: Perps funding rates, explained like you're new here
entry.summary: A funding rate is a recurring payment between long and short perpetual futures traders that keeps a contract's price anchored to the spot market.

entry.title: USDC vs USDC.e vs pUSD: stablecoin naming, demystified
entry.summary: USDC is Circle's native dollar token. USDC.e is a bridged copy from a third-party bridge, not Circle. pUSD is Polymarket's own 1:1-backed settlement token.

entry.title: Prediction markets 101: how prices become probabilities
entry.summary: A prediction market app turns trader demand into a live probability — each contract's price shows what the market believes an event's odds are right now.

entry.title: Swop vs Coinbase Wallet: which one fits everyday payments
entry.summary: Swop and Coinbase Wallet are both self-custodial wallets. They differ on gas fees, chain support, and how each actually handles in-person crypto payments.

entry.title: Crypto tap to pay: how in-person payments work
entry.summary: Crypto tap-to-pay lets you pay in person with NFC or a QR code instead of a card. Here's how the request, price lock, and on-chain settlement actually work.

entry.title: Crypto link in bio: a storefront AI agents can buy from
entry.summary: A crypto link in bio page holds a wallet address and can list real products for sale — including to AI agents that pay automatically over the x402 protocol.

entry.title: What is x402? The payment protocol for AI agents
entry.summary: x402 is an open protocol that lets software pay for API access over HTTP using stablecoins — no accounts, API keys, or credit cards. Here's how it works.

entry.title: Is Swop safe? How self-custody and signing work
entry.summary: You control your Swop wallet: nothing moves without your approval, you can export your private key, and its AI agent can propose trades but never sign for you.

entry.title: ERC-8196 in production: how Swop polices its trading agent
entry.summary: ERC-8196 standardizes policy-bound AI agent wallets. Here's how Swop's trading agent runs under an ERC-8196-inspired policy layer — versioned policies, EIP-712 owner signatures, and a hash-chained audit log.

entry.title: Gasless crypto: how sponsored transactions work
entry.summary: A gasless crypto wallet sponsors your network fees so you don't need to hold SOL or ETH just to transact. Here's how sponsored transactions actually work.

entry.title: Swop vs Phantom: which Solana wallet fits you
entry.summary: Swop and Phantom are both self-custodial Solana wallets. They differ on gas fees, chain support, in-person payments, and how their AI agents confirm trades.

entry.title: Best self-custody wallet for Solana: what it means
entry.summary: A self-custody wallet gives you sole control of the keys that move your Solana tokens, so no exchange can freeze or access them. Here's what to check first.

entry.title: Agentic trading is live: your wallet can now hold an opinion
entry.summary: Astro reads the book, sizes the position, and asks before it acts. How Swop built an agent for spot, perps, and prediction markets that confirms before it moves money.
